feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope of responsibility is well evidenced. It reads professionally and has good strategic/technical breadth, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: large-scale Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI search work show meaningful ownership and modern capability.  
- Writing is polished overall: concise, professional, and easy to scan, with good use of specifics like “10,000+ page website” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve readability and save space.  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“front-end” vs other compounds, “organization-wide”/“member-facing” style); “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most relevant differentiators: public-sector scale, platform modernization, governance, and analytics.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language such as “leading” or “driving” to emphasize ownership.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years guiding web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise platforms, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV and keep parallel phrasing in the list of capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The long list of functions repeats several items already covered in Core Competencies.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scanability and reduce repetition.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and sharpen broad items:
  Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “website” with “web” for a more senior, enterprise-level tone.
- Change “content experiences” to “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest value: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, communications, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps heavily with Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful as a footer.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed X to achieve Y,” and replace vague phrasing like “designed for continued campaign growth” with “scalable for future campaign phases.”
- Standardize style and hyphenation: “AI-enabled,” “bill-level,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consider “Hybrid Search Experience” as a clearer title.
- Where possible, add one concrete signal of scope or value (audience, platform, campaign purpose, or business outcome).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing unique projects here and removing those already well represented above.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Make it more outcome-oriented and frame it as post-director consulting leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with the consulting mandate and seniority: “Advising NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper results-focused bullets; e.g., “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member toolkits.”
- Combine systems/governance language: “Improved cross-channel communications operations through analytics, workflow design, governance, and usability standards across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but make it outcome-led if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy content.” Add metrics/deliverables if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS development, front-end implementation, and technical troubleshooting” may duplicate skills/older execution-heavy roles; keep this item more strategic.
- Microsites and AI search already appear in Recent Projects, so avoid repeating the same wording.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor achievement and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, deliverability, or campaign impact metrics for email/social if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets to action + result: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, expanding capacity for advocacy programming and event production”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; differentiate this entry through enterprise ownership and transformation.
- Video-programming language partially repeats older NACo entries; emphasize studio buildout and organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with sharper action verbs and any measurable growth.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more impact-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here to preserve progression.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this entry as expansion/scaling rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, differentiated terms tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Content operations and governance leadership” to avoid vague wording.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “messaging,” “planning,” and “leadership” styles.
- If space allows, align one phrase to measurable scale from recent work, e.g., “Enterprise web and content strategy for 10,000+ page platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too long and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. This topline item should be tighter, more senior, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool dump to a focused capability line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they read as secondary versus recent Drupal-led work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-facing sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool lists duplicate the Technical + IT section; keep this version more strategic and selective.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and position it as strategic capability, not just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, stronger phrasing like “search, content and conversion performance analysis” if accurate.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • Search, content and user-performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory below.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; avoid repeating both verbatim.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and higher-value production capabilities rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Tighten and elevate the list: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event production workflows**
- If space allows, add one stronger capability instead of “editing,” e.g. **Run-of-show and technical production coordination** or **Advocacy video programming**
- Keep terms consistent with recent experience: align with “broadcast-quality in-house video studio” and “livestream operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially duplicate **Core Competencies: Multimedia production and livestream operations**
- “Video production and editing” is already supported by older roles; avoid over-weighting it unless tied to recent studio leadership or event delivery scale

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers to show depth, not just familiarity: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use “CMS & Web Platforms” if you want a clearer heading.
- If no qualifiers are added, consider shortening to just the top 3–4 most relevant platforms to avoid looking like a generic keyword list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages may feel lower-value unless supported elsewhere by project or implementation context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function for clarity: “Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager” and “Serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner
- If accurate, add scope/level in parentheses to avoid sounding junior, e.g. “GitHub Actions (deployment automation)” or “Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless this section is strictly implementation-focused

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped around systems you actively build or lead.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools first; if Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier are the real automation stack, keep those prominent and consider dropping one weaker PM tool.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to outcomes rather than listing everything, e.g. “Built workflow automation and cross-team coordination systems using Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis in multiple sections.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if collaboration platforms are genuinely part of your systems leadership story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/operational context shown elsewhere in the CV. It should signal enterprise email platform ownership without repeating newsletter management already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use: **Enterprise email campaign management, audience journeys, and member communications**
- Keep it platform-focused; let the work experience carry outcomes like audience size, newsletter cadence, and channel leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in roles [2] and [3]
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item specifically tool/platform-oriented

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it more capability-led and slightly more senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI/reporting dashboards • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing)**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **KPI/reporting dashboards** to sound more outcome-oriented and executive-relevant.
- Replace bare “SEO” with **SEO/performance analysis** to show applied use, not just familiarity.
- Consider ordering by strategic weight and recency: analytics stack first, then optimization capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**. Consider trimming one section or differentiating this one as tools-only.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere in recent roles; keep it only if you can support it with a project or outcome.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and video.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, email/social volume, or team support.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates, supported a major website refresh, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If space allows, split into 2 bullets for readability rather than one dense paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” and workflow improvements overlap with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as the origin/build phase, not ongoing program leadership.
- Avoid broad claims about governance/strategy here; those are stronger and more credible in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities at NACo.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: audience size, number of episodes, stakeholder groups served, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or program visibility.
- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Supported program and policy teams through research-driven innovation projects and created multimedia content that expanded NACo’s digital storytelling capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later roles; keep this item focused on research support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since later entries show the progression into formal digital leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, with concise labels and no broad capability statements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
